Vanessa —

Thanks for sending. We reviewed internally and Harrison Law prepared a counter-redline. Two quick items up front: Cobalt cannot accept an "unlimited damages" bucket that requires third-party forensics as a gating condition without a clearer SLA on evidence access and timing. In practice our procurement/compliance teams need to be able to trigger a preservation and get rights to forensic outputs within 30 days.

Key asks from Cobalt:
- Replace "unlimited damages" with "no cap on damages" for trade-secret misappropriation, but allow Cobalt to seek injunctive relief before damages are assessed.
- Forensic access: Redwood must cooperate with Cobalt's chosen digital forensics vendor or provide equivalent exportable audit logs within 14 business days of request.
- Burden of proof: Cobalt is willing to accept a defined standard (preponderance of evidence) for triggering the uncapped remedy if forensic evidence is produced.

I've attached our redline: Cobalt_Redline_v2.docx. Please have your counsel comment on the forensic access timing and whether a mutually agreeable vendor list is acceptable.

Subject: RE: Liability carve-out language for trade secrets — redlines attached

Amy / team —

Appreciate the quick review. A few legal positions from Redwood's side and a counter-proposal to keep this narrow and operationally viable:

Counter-proposal (high level):
1) Carve-out triggers: uncapped damages only where (i) the claimant establishes misappropriation of Trade Secrets under the Uniform Trade Secrets Act (or equivalent), and (ii) Redwood's audit logs or mutually agreed forensic report demonstrate exfiltration of Data originating from the claimant's account to an identified external actor.

2) Forensic cooperation: Redwood will cooperate in good faith with Cobalt's chosen vendor but cannot be forced to use an external vendor to run inside-Runtime forensics on customer-hosted infra. Redwood will provide exportable raw audit logs, session metadata, and a reasonable redaction process for PII. We propose 20 business days for log export and initial report, with an option to expedite at Cobalt's cost.

3) Injunctive relief: preserve right to seek injunctive relief before damages are liquidated.

4) Proof standard: preponderance of evidence.

We also want to limit this exception to breaches arising from Redwood infrastructure and code (not third-party plugins or customer-configured connectors), to avoid open-ended exposure. If Cobalt needs expansion for hybrid infra, that materially changes risk and price.

Commercial ask: If Redwood is asked to accept uncapped exposure with a 20-day forensic window and the limited scope above, Sales has asked RevOps to price a one-time indemnity reserve. Marissa / Vanessa, can you confirm expected concession range so I can include a note for Laura's approval?

Proposed clause snippet (for insertion into MSA):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), the liability cap shall not apply to damages resulting from (a) wilful and knowing misappropriation of Trade Secrets as defined herein, and (b) unauthorized exfiltration of Customer Data that is demonstrated by Redwood's audit logs or a mutually agreed forensic report identifying Data transfer to an external actor. Prior to seeking damages, the parties shall cooperate to preserve relevant evidence and may seek equitable relief. Redwood shall provide exportable audit logs within 20 business days of a written request; expedited production may be available at Customer's expense."

Laura, please advise if GC is comfortable with the 20 business day window and the scope carve-in.

Thanks,
Rishi
Deputy GC | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Putting Rishi's counter in plain English: Redwood can agree to a narrowly tailored removal of the liability cap for confirmed trade-secret misappropriation where demonstrable forensic evidence ties the event to our service, with exportable logs and a defined timeline. Redwood requests 20 business days to produce logs and a carve-out limited to Redwood-managed infra. Cobalt asked for 14 business days and the ability to use your vendor; Rishi's text attempts to split the difference with an expedite option at Cobalt's cost.

Commercially: Marissa and I ran the numbers — if Redwood accepts the 20 business day window and the limited infra scope, RevOps recommends a one-time credit up to 2.5% of the first-year committed spend in exchange for the exception. That concession balances residual risk and keeps legal exposure contained. If Cobalt insists on 14 days or uncapped scope (hybrid infra), we'll need to revisit pricing (likely higher).
